sections.h2: How has Nicholasville grown, and what does it mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Nicholasville is the county seat of Jessamine County and a home rule city south of Lexington. It counted 28,015 residents in 2010 and 31,093 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimated 33,857 on July 1, 2025, a rise of 8.8 percent over the 2020 base. Between 1970 and 2020 the population grew by about 440 percent, which makes it the tenth most populous city in Kentucky.

Growth like that means a lot of the housing is relatively recent and a lot of owners are commuters. The 2020-2024 Census figures show 12,131 households, an owner-occupied rate of 58.2 percent, a median home value of $226,800 and a mean commute of 24 minutes.

sections.h2: What is the setting of a Nicholasville house?
sections.html:
The town was founded in 1798 and incorporated in 1837, named for a colonel who helped shape Kentucky's first constitution. Downtown sits about six miles south of the Fayette County line, and the city covers roughly 13 square miles of land. A partly channelized stream called Town Fork runs underneath downtown and drains to Jessamine Creek, and there are small artificial ponds such as Lake Mingo.

The Bluegrass climate is humid subtropical at its northern edge, with hot, humid summers, cool winters and four distinct seasons. Camp Nelson National Monument is close by, the Young House is on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Kentucky Wine and Vine Fest was named the official wine festival of Kentucky by the General Assembly in 2014.

  • Nicholasville is a logistics and commuter link between Lexington and Garrard County.
  • Jessamine County Schools provides public education, including Nicholasville, Brookside, Red Oak, Rosenwald-Dunbar and Hattie C. Warner elementary schools.
  • City government is a commission of a mayor and four commissioners, elected at large, who also run city departments.

sections.h2: Who handles code complaints and permits in Nicholasville?
sections.html:
Nicholasville has its own Code Enforcement office at 717 N. Main Street, and complaints go in through a form on the city website. A Code Enforcement Board also hears matters, and residents can apply to serve on it. If you have received a notice about tall grass, debris or an unsafe structure, answer it before you list or accept an offer.

For building and electrical permits, ask the city Planning and Zoning office which approvals your project needs, and keep copies of finished permits to hand to a buyer. Unpermitted work is a common reason a conventional sale stalls, so tell a buyer about it up front.

sections.h2: What does the Jessamine County Clerk do when a Nicholasville house sells?
sections.html:
The Jessamine County Clerk records deeds and mortgages and keeps the county's property records. The main office is at 101 North Main Street in Nicholasville and is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; a Wilmore branch keeps shorter hours. The county number is (859) 885-4161.

On a sale, the clerk collects Kentucky's transfer tax before accepting the deed. KRS 142.050 sets the rate at fifty cents for every $500 of value, charged to the seller, and the clerk keeps five percent of what is collected as a fee and passes the rest to the county treasurer.

Some transfers are exempt, including conveyances between parent and child for only nominal consideration, sales for delinquent taxes and transfers in a foreclosure or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

sections.h2: What should a Nicholasville owner know about property tax?
sections.html:
The Jessamine County PVA assesses real estate for the county, and its site announced that the homestead and disability exemption for 2025-2026 is $49,100. Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, can apply through the PVA, and the exemption lowers the taxable value rather than the bill itself.

On a sale, the year's tax is normally split between you and the buyer at closing, so ask the closing agent how the proration will be computed. If a bill on an inherited house has gone unpaid, ask the County Clerk's delinquent tax desk for the amount owed before you agree on a closing date.

sections.h2: When is a cash offer a good fit for a Nicholasville house?
sections.html:
It suits a house where time matters more than the last few thousand dollars. A commuter town with 33,857 residents has plenty of buyers, but a house with problems can still sit.

  • An inherited house where the heirs live out of state and do not want to manage repairs.
  • A rental whose tenant has left, leaving work to be done before it can be shown.
  • A house with an open code complaint or unpermitted work.
  • An owner relocating on a short timeline to or from the Lexington area.

Ask for written terms, check the net against a listing after repairs and agent costs, and have the title company confirm the payoff before you accept.

faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 31,093 residents in 2020 and estimated 33,857 for July 1, 2025. The city has about 14.6 square miles of land.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Nicholasville house?
faqs.a: At the Jessamine County Clerk, 101 North Main Street in Nicholasville, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The clerk collects the transfer tax before it records the deed.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a $226,800 sale?
faqs.a: The tax is $227. It is fifty cents for each $500 of value, rounded up to 454 units, and the seller pays it under KRS 142.050.

faqs.q: How do I report or answer a code complaint in Nicholasville?
faqs.a: Use the form on the city's Code Enforcement page or visit 717 N. Main Street. If you have received a notice, respond to it before listing before you agree to a closing date.

faqs.q: Is there a property tax break for older homeowners in Jessamine County?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older, or with a disability, can apply to the PVA for the homestead exemption, which was $49,100 for 2025-2026. It reduces assessed value rather than the bill itself.
